description: Address, bank account, phone number, tax number and proof of income are mutually prerequisite in most destination countries. The loop is broken by whichever institution will bend first.
energy_note: Competent, employed, and unable to open a door.

description: Breaking the loop usually means paying for short-term accommodation at several times the market rent while queuing for everything else.
money_note: Weeks of short-let at a premium.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the deposit nobody has yet
description: Tenancies commonly want first month, last month and a deposit up front - before a salary has been paid, and from money that had to be moved out of Iran informally (see FIN-002).

aspect: EXAMPLE - the sanctions screen fires on arrival
description: The bank that finally opens the account runs the same sanctions screen that closes Iranian accounts elsewhere, so the one institution that broke the loop may also be the one that exits the relationship a year later (FIN-001).

aspect: EXAMPLE - no guarantor in the country
description: Where a local guarantor is required, an immigrant by definition has none, and commercial guarantor services charge a percentage of annual rent.

aspect: SCENARIO - eleven days in an Airbnb
description: Omid lands in Toronto on a Tuesday. The bank wants a proof of address; the landlord wants a bank statement and a credit check; the phone company wants an address and a credit check. He spends eleven nights at CAD 140 and signs a lease at 30% above market with six months' rent up front, because it is the only one that does not ask.
energy_note: Paying a premium for the privilege of not existing yet.
